chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the conduct of the Imam in the land that was conquered after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he said: 'Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) conducted himself among the people of Iraq with a conduct that is an example for all other lands.'

And he said: 'Indeed, the land tax (jizyah) is not lifted from them, and rather the jizyah is the stipend (ata') of the Muhajirun (Emigrants), and the alms-tax (sadaqat) is for its people, whom Allah named in His Book; they have nothing in the jizyah.'

Then he said: 'How broad is justice! Indeed, the people expand (prosper) when justice is done among them, and the sky sends down its provision, and the earth brings forth its blessings, by the permission of Allah, the Exalted.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the distinction between jizyah and sadaqah in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes the conduct of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) in Iraq as the definitive model for governance and taxation across all lands, clarifying that jizyah functions as a stipend for the Muhajirun while sadaqah is reserved for the specific recipients mentioned in the Quran. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the distinct fiscal roles of these two levies, correcting common misconceptions about their distribution. It concludes by linking just administration to cosmic blessings, illustrating how equitable governance invites divine provision and earthly abundance.
